title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s response explains how it plans to create clear rules and standards for artificial intelligence, focusing on safety, fairness, and accountability. It also outlines funding, collaboration with industry, and ongoing consultation to help AI systems meet the public’s expectations and protect users.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in the UK’s qualifications system, aiming to keep exams fair, transparent and secure. It will develop rules, monitor AI tools in test‑taking, and work with educators, tech firms and regulators to manage risks and safeguard assessment quality.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how AI systems use copyrighted materials and evaluates the legal, economic, and societal effects. It provides guidance to stakeholders on balancing innovation with copyright protection and offers recommendations to mitigate risks.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has released its response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining plans to strengthen regulation, boost innovation, and protect public safety. It emphasises that the UK will take decisive action to keep pace with AI advances while ensuring ethical and competitive standards.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the terms of reference and frequently asked questions for a committee reviewing how artificial intelligence affects public standards. It defines the committee’s scope, objectives, and procedures for evaluating AI’s impact on public policy and standards.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence. In its submission, CSPL outlines its views and recommendations for how AI should be regulated and monitored to ensure responsible development and use.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document explains how artificial intelligence is changing the way medical products are regulated and shows how regulators plan to apply the principles laid out in the AI White Paper. It focuses on ensuring safety, transparency, and accountability for AI‑driven medical devices by adopting risk‑based guidelines, strengthening data governance, and fostering collaboration between regulators, industry, and patients.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our defence organization the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI leader for its size. It sets a roadmap for integrating AI across defence operations, enhancing capabilities while upholding high standards of trust and accountability.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan shows how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to take advantage of AI opportunities. It also explains how the department will manage and reduce any potential risks associated with those technologies.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyright-protected works are being used to train and improve AI systems, assessing current practices and challenges. It also examines compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act, outlining progress made and future steps for balancing creativity with data access.
